summary: David P. Chandler studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. A scholar of history and archaeology, he held academic posts at Cornell, Johns Hopkins, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

David P. Jackson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, and held posts including C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and also studied under Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley, a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He served as associate professor at Naropa University and co-director at the Nitartha Institute.

David Pingree specialized in Indology and the history of archaeology. He earned his bachelor's and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto E. Neugebauer, and held posts at Chicago, Brown, and Cornell.

David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD), and served as department chair during his 1969–2000 career at McMaster University.

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the National University of Singapore (PhD), holding posts at NUS, Bunkyo University, and Xavier University.

David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of Colorado Boulder and Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later holding positions at Indiana University, Washington University, and Alberta.
David Reigle is a researcher in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at Asian Humanities Press.

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned BA, MA, and Litt.D. degrees from Cambridge, holding academic appointments at Cambridge, the University of Michigan, and Harvard University.
David Ruddell was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a sinologist who studied at Stanford University and earned his PhD from Harvard University. Since 1996, he has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he has served as dean of Humanities and professor.

David Seyfort Ruegg specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jean Filliozat and Louis Renou, he held professorships at Leiden University, the University of Hamburg, and SOAS University of London.

David Shea was an Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin from 1793 to 1798 and later served as an assistant professor at the East India Company College (1826–1836).

David Slakter specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his master's degree at the University of Liverpool under the supervision of Christopher Bartley and was appointed assistant professor at Camden County College in 2024.
David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

David Teplitz was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from Northwestern University and a Ph.D. from the American Academy of Asian Studies. He also taught at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

David Tracy is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at Catholic University of America before serving from 1969 to 2006 at the University of Chicago.

David W. Chappell was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He earned degrees from Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale (PhD), serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1971–2000) and teaching at Soka University of America.

David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, completing his PhD under the supervision of James Robson.
